Conflict: Material and Design Agent recommends recycled post-consumer ABS with structural ribbing, while In-Service Agent rejects this due to concerns about lower drop and impact resistance compared to unreinforced polycarbonate, and Circularity Agent demands a monomaterial polymer housing to maximize recycling quality.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; In-Service Agent; Circularity Agent
Decision: Recycled post-consumer thermoplastic (rPCR-ABS) with molded-in structural ribbing
Rationale: Using rPCR-ABS with structural ribbing balances the regulatory requirement for recycled content (h) and lightweight design (t) while structural ribbing ensures engineering feasibility by providing the necessary drop resistance without relying on non-recyclable glass-fiber reinforcements.

Conflict: Material and Design Agent recommends threaded metal fasteners with brass inserts to enable non-destructive disassembly, whereas Manufacture Agent rejects this due to increased assembly cycle times and labor costs compared to ultrasonic welding.
Agents Involved: Material and Design Agent; Manufacture Agent
Decision: Threaded metal fasteners with brass inserts and standard Torx screws
Rationale: Threaded fasteners with brass inserts enable non-destructive disassembly and re-assembly, which is a key regulatory requirement under ESPR Annex I (b) for ease of repair and maintenance, overriding the manufacturer's cost-saving preference for permanent ultrasonic welding.

Conflict: In-Service Agent recommends a brushless DC motor to maximize durability and energy efficiency, whereas Manufacture Agent rejects this due to the high manufacturing environmental footprint and hazardous waste generated during rare-earth magnet extraction.
Decision: Brushless DC (BLDC) motor with easily extractable neodymium magnets and separable windings
Rationale: A brushless motor significantly improves durability (a) and energy efficiency (g) during service, which are core ESPR parameters; the manufacturing and environmental footprint concerns are mitigated by designing the motor with easily extractable magnets to support high-purity recycling (d).

Conflict: In-Service Agent recommends passive conduction via internal heat sinks and a completely sealed housing to prevent dust ingress, whereas Circularity Agent rejects any design using thermal potting compounds or non-separable components that hinder material recovery.
Decision: Passive cooling via integrated housing vents and a detachable recycled aluminum heat sink
Rationale: This approach avoids thermal potting compounds which are highly detrimental to recycling (e) and generate hazardous waste (r), while using a detachable aluminum heat sink to provide sufficient thermal dissipation without relying on active fans that draw in dust, thus balancing durability (a) and recyclability (d).

Conflict: Circularity Agent recommends a highly modular architecture with separate, easily swappable modules to facilitate repair and reuse, whereas Manufacture Agent rejects this because modular connections increase spatial requirements, tool weight, and manufacturing costs.
Decision: Highly modular architecture with separate, plug-and-play functional modules (battery, motor, switch, gearbox)
Rationale: A highly modular architecture is required to comply with ESPR Annex I (b) ease of repair and (c) ease of upgrading and remanufacturing, which are non-negotiable regulatory requirements that override manufacturing cost and complexity concerns.

Conflict: In-Service Agent recommends a removable, standardized slide-on battery pack to ensure portability and ease of replacement, whereas Manufacture Agent rejects this in favor of a corded direct-mains power supply to minimize the high carbon footprint of battery manufacturing.
Decision: Easily removable, standardized slide-on/clip-in Lithium-ion battery pack using standard cylindrical cells
Rationale: A corded power supply fails the fundamental functional performance and conditions for use (s) of a cordless screwdriver, making it commercially and functionally unfeasible. To comply with ESPR Annex I (s) and ensure engineering feasibility, a battery is required. By making the battery pack easily removable and standardized, we satisfy ease of repair (b), ease of upgrading/reuse (c), and safe removal of substances of concern (f) before end-of-life recycling (d).
